item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00497","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C22","C01","C17"],"selected_candidate_label":"C22","confidence":0.73,"relationship_type":"structural_functional_template","rationale":"C22 plausibly supplied a material structural template. Both proclamations invoke the Philippine Trade Act, quote a statutory provision making a Philippine trade benefit depend on a presidentially proclaimed factual condition, recount bilateral Philippine-government information or consultation, and then formally proclaim that the statutory condition exists so the specified customs or tax treatment follows. C01 has similar reciprocity-determination machinery but concerns copyright and lacks the distinctive Philippine trade-law setting. C17 shares customs-entry terminology and date-bounded tariff treatment, but its multipart trade-agreement machinery is substantially different.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"the act of July 5, 1954 ... provides as follows: “The duty-free treatment ... shall apply ... during such period ... as the President may declare by proclamation”","parent_excerpt":"section 505(b) of the Philippine Trade Act of 1946 ... provides as follows: “Whenever the President, after consultation with the President of the Philippines, finds ... he shall so proclaim”","explanation":"Each recites a Philippine Trade Act provision under which a presidential proclamation of a factual condition activates a specified trade or tax consequence."},{"child_excerpt":"do hereby declare and proclaim on the basis of information received from the Government of the Philippines, that United States articles ... will be admitted into the Philippines free of ordinary customs duty","parent_excerpt":"do hereby proclaim that, after consultation with the President of the Philippines, I have found that adequate supplies of copra and coconut oil ... are readily available","explanation":"Both operative clauses turn information obtained from the Philippine government into the formal presidential finding required by the quoted statute."},{"child_excerpt":"entered, or withdrawn from warehouse, in the Philippines for consumption, during the period from July 4, 1954, to December 31, 1955","parent_excerpt":"the processing tax ... will be applicable ... on and after August 27, 1949","explanation":"Both conclude by specifying the customs or tax consequence and its effective period after proclaiming the statutory predicate."}]}
